- [Immediate execution](immediate-execution.md) — left-to-right, no precedence; 2 + 3 × 4 = 20
- [Number presentation](number-presentation.md) — render-time rounding only, 10 sig digits; ÷0 error state
- [Tape](tape.md) — rows only when = computes; token-built expressions; AC keeps tape
- [Memory keys](memory-keys.md) — exact memory; AC keeps it; M+ ends typing; MR acts as entry
---
name: immediate-execution
description: Calculator evaluates strictly left to right with no operator precedence (2 + 3 × 4 = 20); project-wide decision
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 705e51b4-3524-472d-917f-886debebac4a
  modified: 2026-09-13T02:45:59.825Z
---

The calculator uses immediate execution. Each operator key finishes the waiting operation, left to right. No operator precedence: `2 + 3 × 4 =` is `20`.

**Why:** It matches a pocket calculator and keeps the running display honest. The number on screen is always a real result the calculator will use.

**How to apply:** Every future feature (memory keys, percent, sign toggle, backspace, history) must fit this model. Never add a parser or precedence. Decided 2026-09-12.

Parentheses (added 2026-09-12) fit this model: `(` saves the waiting operation on a stack and starts a fresh left-to-right calculation; `)` finishes it and the result becomes the entry; `=` closes any open groups. No expression parsing.
---
name: memory-keys
description: M+/MR/MC behaviour — exact memory value, AC keeps memory, how M+ and MR interact with entry state
metadata:
  type: project
---

Memory keys added 2026-09-12.
- Memory holds the exact value, never rounded. M+ adds the exact displayed value (`0.1 M+ 0.2 M+` holds 0.30000000000000004, shows 0.3).
- `mem-indicator` `data-active` is `true` when memory !== 0. So `5 M+ ± M+` turns it off.
- AC does not clear memory; only MC does. In the error state memory keys are ignored like all keys but AC.
- M+ ends typing: next digit starts a new number. The value stays the entry for a waiting op (`2 + 5 M+ =` is 7).
- MR makes memory the entry, like typing it. Tape shows it via the formatter.

**Why:** Follows [[number-presentation]] and [[immediate-execution]].
**How to apply:** Memory lives outside `state` so `reset()` keeps it.
---
name: number-presentation
description: Rounding is render-time only; max 10 sig digits, no trailing zeros, exp notation at >=1e10 or <1e-9; data-value stays exact
metadata:
  type: project
---

Decided 2026-09-12, holds for the rest of the calculator project.
- Display rounds to at most 10 significant digits, drops trailing zeros and a trailing ".". No thousands separators.
- Exponential notation only when magnitude >= 1e10 or < 1e-9.
- Stored/computed value is never rounded. `data-value` on `calc-display` always carries the exact value.
- While typing, show the entry exactly as typed.
- Division by zero: display `Error`, `data-error="true"`, all keys but clear ignored; clear resets to `0`. `data-error` is always present.

**Why:** Rounding stored values compounds through chains; `2 ÷ 3 × 3 =` must be exactly `2`.
**How to apply:** Never add rounding/cleaning in compute paths; format only in render. Related: [[immediate-execution]].
---
name: tape
description: Running tape of past calculations; which equals presses add a row and how expressions are written
metadata:
  type: project
---

Tape added 2026-09-12. Newest row first; row = expression + result only.
- A row is added only when `=` actually computes: an operation, a repeated `=`, or a group result like `(2 + 3) =`. A lone `5 =` adds nothing. `÷0` adds nothing.
- Expression is built from tokens as keys are pressed, not parsed: operators shown as `+ − × ÷`, numbers via the display formatter, groups as `(3 × 4)`, ± on a group as `-(2 + 3)`. `5 + =` shows `5 + 5`; repeated `=` shows `last result op operand`.
- `tape-result` `data-value` is exact (`String(value)`), text is formatted. AC does not clear the tape; Clear does not touch the display.

**Why:** Keeps the tape honest to [[immediate-execution]] and [[number-presentation]].
**How to apply:** New keys that change the entry must keep `state.tokens` / `state.entryExpr` in sync.

content.text:
Both features work, and all the earlier checks I ran still pass. No regressions turned up. Nothing is committed.

**Keyboard entry** was already built. In a headless browser I checked the digit keys, `.`, `+ - * /`, `Enter`, `=` and `Escape`. `Enter` does not press a button twice when one has focus (click `7`, press `Enter` still shows `7`).

**Scientific panel** is new in `index.html`:
- `key-sci` sits beside MC/MR/M+ and opens a row with `key-sqrt`, `key-square` and `key-recip`. The panel is closed on load.
- Each key acts on the number on the display right away, and the result becomes the entry. `9 √` shows `3`, and `9 + √ =` gives `12`.
- The square root of a negative number and `1/0` show the Error state, the same as dividing by zero.
- The tape writes these as `√9`, `9²` and `1/9`. Groups and negative numbers get brackets: `(3 × 4)²`, `(-3)²`.
- `9 √ =` adds a tape row, just as a group result like `(2 + 3) =` does.
- The panel toggle still works in the Error state, because opening a panel is not a calculation.
- When the panel is open, the tape panel grows to match the calculator's height. The narrow (400px) layout still fits without scrolling sideways.

**Fixed:** my first version showed the panel on page load, because its CSS layout rule overrode `hidden`. I added a rule so `hidden` works, and it now starts closed.

**Checked again, all passing:** left-to-right order (`2 + 3 × 4 = 20`), exact values (`2 ÷ 3 × 3 = 2`), 10-digit display, divide-by-zero Error and AC, brackets, tape rows (including repeated `=`), ±, and memory (exact value kept, AC leaves it alone).

I added a memory note on how the scientific keys behave.
